analysis.title: Americas Banks: Regional. Handbook: Analyzing key industry trends. Focus on NII growth, deposit costs, loan growth and adjusted capital
key_insights: Regional bank NII (FTE) rose 1.8% QoQ on average in 3Q26, led by NIM expansion of 2bps and earning-asset growth. Loan yields rose 3bps on fixed-rate repricing, securities yields rose 8bps and deposit costs rose 5bps.

Consensus expects regional bank NII up about 1.2% in 4Q26 (about 2.5% above guidance or implied guidance) and NIM up about 4bps in 4Q26 and about 11bps by 4Q27. Largest expected 2027 NIM expansion is at KEY (+27bps), ZION (+23bps) and FCNCA, smallest at MTB, HBAN and TFC.
Most banks assume one more 25bp Fed hike in December 2026 and two in 2027. ZION assumes three hikes (Dec, Mar, Jun), RF assumes flat rates, and HBAN moved from four-to-seven cuts to one-to-two hikes.

Cumulative down deposit betas averaged 50% in 3Q26 on 175bps of cuts. Deposit costs rose in anticipation of hikes, led by ZION (+15bps), FHN (+12bps) and FITB (+11bps). Consensus implies betas starting slow at 43% in 4Q26 and reaching 54% by YE27, which management commentary (BKU ~80%, FHN ~60%, HBAN 50-60%, RF mid-to-high 30s) shows is not uniform.

Cumulative down loan betas averaged about 29% against about 45% net floating-rate sensitivity, a gap of roughly 15 points that GS attributes to fixed-rate repricing. GS expects beta outperformance to continue at a slower pace. About 43% of earning assets are estimated to be floating rate.

Receive-fixed swaps on loans total about $217bn notional and are a drag on NII of about $216mn in 3Q26 rising to about $406mn in 4Q26E. GS estimates the net NII effect with floating-rate loan tailwinds as about +4% in 4Q26 across the group.

Loan growth: regional EOP loans were about flat QoQ and up 3.9% YoY in 3Q26. C&I (+9.6% YoY) is strongest and auto (-5.9%) weakest. Street expects about 0.9% QoQ growth in 4Q26 and about 4.2% in 2027. MTB is the one bank flagging deceleration into 2027 on macro uncertainty and slower CRE growth.

Spotlight on capital: banks expect Basel 3 Endgame to add about 90bps to adjusted CET1, but fully using it would put most banks below a ~7% TCE ratio. Managing to an average ~7.6% TCE, GS sees most banks able to return capital ahead of consensus, with the biggest gaps at FCNCA (+$2.2bn), TFC (+$2.0bn) and CFG (+$984mn) and the smallest at FITB, FHN and ALLY ($0).

Much of the upside to capital return depends on securities accretion (AOCI earnback). Excluding it, GS sees upside mainly at FCNCA (+$1.8bn), SYF (+$730mn) and MTB (+$522mn), and far fewer banks can exceed consensus.

Credit: regional bank NCOs averaged about 33bps in 3Q26, NPLs fell 3bps to about 71bps and the ACL ratio slipped 4bps to 1.36%. Implied 4Q26 NCO guidance is about 30bps by the exhibit and about 34bps by the text, flat versus consensus.

Consumer finance: card DQs were 3.71% (up ~21bps QoQ, down ~18bps YoY) and NCOs fell ~38bps YoY. Issuers guide to about 4.86% card losses in 2026. ALLY's 2026 retail auto vintage DQs track above 2024 and 2025 at T+2 but GS expects less underperformance given originations and S-tier mix.
Consumer finance NII rose about 4.8% QoQ in 3Q26 and 6.3% YoY. Card loan yields rose about 33bps QoQ. Consensus expects 2027 NII growth of about 5.8% led by AXP (+8.4%) and ALLY (+6.4%).

2027 consensus EPS was stable after 3Q26 results. FCNCA saw the largest positive PPNR revision (+10%) and TFC the largest negative (-5%, lower NII). In consumer finance, BFH rose 2% while COF and ALLY fell 2%.

Consensus expects 2027 ROTCE for banks about 0.3 points below management targets on average (16.8% vs 17.1% assumed). Largest gaps: FHN consensus 10.0% against a 15%+ target, RF consensus 21.1% against 16-18%.
Private credit exposure as a share of loans is highest at KEY (9.8%) and CFG (4.8%) and lowest at BKU (0.4%). NDFI loan growth across commercial banks is moderating to 16% YoY in 3Q26.

market_movers.rationale: PT based on 11.5x 2027E EPS. 2028 EPS cut to $250 from $260 on credit and cost views, 2026/2027 EPS kept at $210/$230. Also the largest buyback upside vs consensus (+$2.2bn).
PT on 21.5x 2027E EPS, down from 26x on mortgage market views. EPS estimates for 2026/2027/2028 changed to $0.55/$0.60/$0.80 from $0.53/$0.50/$0.60.

earnings_insights: Regional bank 3Q26 NII (FTE) rose 1.8% QoQ on average (reported). Average NIM was 3.27% (reported), up 2bps QoQ.
Visible Alpha consensus (estimate, not a print) expects 4Q26 regional NII up about 1.2% QoQ and NIM up about 4bps, then about 11bps higher by 4Q27 versus 3Q26.

Consumer finance 3Q26 NII rose about 4.8% QoQ and about 6.3% YoY (reported) with average NIM about 11.1%. Consensus (estimate) expects 4Q26 NII growth of about 1.4%, led by SYF (+3.1%) and ALLY (+2.0%).

GS 2027 EPS estimates versus Visible Alpha consensus (core EPS for CFG, FCNCA and TFC): FCNCA $230.00 vs $217.09 (+6%), ZION $7.35 vs $6.99 (+5%), MTB $19.91 vs $20.97 (-5%). Consumer finance: COF $22.00 vs $23.70 (-7%), ALLY $5.28 vs $6.01 (-12%). All are forecasts.
Post-3Q26 consensus 2027 EPS revisions (estimates): FCNCA +9%, BFH +2%, COF -2%, ALLY -2%, TFC -2%. The group average was unchanged.

Company guidance cited: AXP FY26 reported EPS guide raised to $18.30-$18.60 and adjusted EPS to $17.60-$17.90 (guidance, not reported). SYF expects diluted EPS near $9.50 for 2026. BFH FY26 net credit loss guide improved to 6.9%-7.0% from 7.0%-7.1%.
4Q26 NII guidance: CFG up ~2.5%-3% QoQ, FITB up 2.5%-3.5%, RF up 1%-2%, TFC $3.65bn-$3.70bn, MTB $1.83bn-$1.85bn, FCNCA $1.70bn-$1.77bn, BKU ~$265mn. All are company guidance.
GS estimates regional bank ROTCE of about 15.1% in 2026E, and consensus expects about 7.4% YoY core PPNR growth in FY26.

risk_factors: Basel 3 Endgame may not be finalized this quarter, and using its full CET1 benefit would push most banks below ~7% TCE.
Capital return upside depends heavily on anticipated securities accretion, and excluding it fewer banks can beat consensus.
Deposit competition and customers asking for higher rates ahead of hikes could push betas above the 43%-54% consensus path (FITB flags larger or more persistent hikes pushing betas higher).
FCNCA downside risks: credit deterioration in SVB-ID, general office and small equipment finance portfolios, and a more dovish rate environment.
RKT downside risks: sustained pressure on gain-on-sale spreads, elevated competition and an inflated cost base if market demand falls.
MTB flags 2027 loan growth deceleration on macro uncertainty and slower CRE growth. HBAN and FHB loan growth also lean on mergers and seasonality.
ALLY's 2026 auto vintage DQs track above 2024 and 2025 at T+2, and auto 30+ DQs rose YoY at TFC, HBAN, ALLY, PNC and CFG.
Private credit and NDFI exposure, notably KEY at 9.8% of loans and CFG at 4.8%.

Exhibit 24 compares cumulative loan beta of about 29% against about 45% net floating-rate sensitivity, a gap of roughly 15 points.
Exhibit 44 shows consensus interest-bearing deposit costs rising about 30bps from 3Q26 to 4Q27, with cumulative beta reaching 54%.
Exhibit 94 shows regional bank average ACL at 1.36% in 3Q26, down from a peak of 1.52%.
Exhibit 55 shows consumer finance IB deposit costs of 3.36% in 3Q26 with consensus rising to about 3.65% by 4Q27.

tension_points.bull_case: Managing to a ~7.6% average TCE, most banks have ample buyback capacity and can return capital ahead of consensus, with the largest gaps at FCNCA (+$2.2bn), TFC (+$2.0bn) and CFG (+$984mn).
tension_points.bear_case: A big driver is anticipated securities accretion. Excluding it, fewer banks can exceed consensus and ALLY, FHN and FITB have little or no upside.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Fully using the Basel capital benefit would put most banks below a ~7% TCE ratio, the level investors and rating agencies are gravitating towards.

tension_points.bull_case: Consensus has betas starting slow at 43% in 4Q26 and reaching 54% by YE27, while loan betas have beaten net floating-rate sensitivity by about 15 points on fixed-rate repricing.
tension_points.bear_case: Deposit costs already rose 5bps in 3Q26 as depositors asked for rate, and banks guide to betas from mid-30s (RF) to about 60% (FHN), with BKU recalling 80% in the last hiking cycle.
tension_points.what_invalidates: More persistent or larger rate increases could gradually push deposit beta higher as customer pricing expectations adjust (FITB).

theme_stances.key_argument: Most banks can buy back more stock than consensus assumes, though securities accretion drives much of the upside.
theme_stances.evidence: most banks have ample buyback capacity and appear to be able to return capital

theme_stances.key_argument: NII is expected to improve into 4Q on NIM expansion, earning-asset growth, rate hikes and fixed-rate repricing.
theme_stances.evidence: NII expected to improve into 4Q, driven by continued NIM expansion and AEA growth

theme_stances.key_argument: Bank NCOs and NPLs are stable to lower and 4Q NCO guidance is flat versus consensus, with card losses trending down.
theme_stances.evidence: Credit performance relatively strong for banks in 2026
